title: Gearhart v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC found the complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1.a because the minister with standing failed to notify the PCA Clerk within BCO 43-3’s 30-day window and did not later give an unqualified ratification; because the complaint could not be put in order, it was dismissed. No merits disposition was reached.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed the complaint against Chicago Metro Presbytery as administratively out of order because the minister with standing did not file or ratify it within the required time. The SJC reached no merits.
summary: An unsigned complaint challenging a January 21 presbytery action was sent to the PCA Clerk by someone without standing. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1.a and dismissed it: the minister with standing failed to notify the Clerk within BCO 43-3’s 30-day window, and his later e-mail was not an unqualified ratification. Because the complaint could not be put in order, the SJC reached no merits. The decision illustrates strict filing and ratification requirements.

sources.supports: Identity as case 2015-02; SJC decision on complaint dated April 29, 2015; administrative disposition; filing defect, BCO 43-3 deadline, no unqualified ratification, and dismissal.

No merits ruling appears.
